current.title: ARROW 2026.11 · A New Workspace
current.summary: ARROW has been rebuilt across its five centers, with redesigned interfaces, deeper customization, a new widget dashboard, better planning, and RAVIN available alongside your work.

groups.label: A redesigned ARROW
items: Orbit, RAVIN, Relay, Waypoint, and Atlas now share a more consistent, connected ARROW experience.
Five interface identities give the entire workspace a distinct look: Core, Bloom, Haven, Atelier, and Pulse.
Each identity changes more than its colors, with its own navigation, layouts, panels, and presentation across supported centers.
Navigation, controls, spacing, typography, and surfaces have been refined throughout ARROW.
Workspaces now adapt more cleanly to smaller screens, including redesigned mobile navigation where needed.

groups.label: Appearance and personalization
items: Explore each of the five identities in a live interface preview before applying it.
Preview home and conversation layouts to see how your chosen identity feels across ARROW.
Choose a coordinated color palette for each identity, with colors saved separately for each one.
Create a custom accent color using a color picker or an exact HEX value.
Use one shared Light, Dark, or System appearance preference across ARROW's centers.
Refined color contrast, accent handling, and appearance consistency make buttons and text easier to read.
Adjust motion preferences in ARROW's appearance controls, including reduced-motion support.

groups.label: Orbit and the new Dashboard
items: Switch between Orbit's interactive world and a full Dashboard built for everyday work.
Build a dashboard from a widget library with tasks, upcoming events, weather, chats, notes, RAVIN, focus tools, and more.
Add, remove, move, and resize widgets directly on a placement grid, with previews that show where each widget fits.
Choose from Balanced, School, Focus, Communication, and Blank Canvas dashboard starting layouts.
Save personal dashboard layouts and presets, with ARROW account synchronization where available.
Complete tasks, capture quick notes, and open relevant ARROW tools directly from supported widgets.
Use a richer weather view with current conditions, an hourly forecast, and a seven-day outlook.
Find weather by ZIP code or city, or choose approximate browser location when you want to.
Orbit's command panel and quick locations have been simplified for quicker navigation, including improved keyboard shortcuts.

groups.label: Waypoint, rebuilt for planning
items: Waypoint's Today screen now emphasizes actual tasks instead of oversized decorative cards.
Filter your tasks by Open, All, or Done, with clear progress and due-date information.
Use Capture to turn free-form thoughts into organized suggestions with RAVIN.
Review, edit, and select Capture suggestions before any changes are applied to your workspace.
Move between six focused areas: Today, Capture, Plans, Calendar, Direction, and Review.
Keep projects, future tasks, goals, scheduled events, and saved notes visible in their relevant sections.
Preview proposed weekly schedules before making planning decisions.
Enjoy cleaner layout density, clearer labels, improved mobile navigation, and more consistent ARROW themes.

groups.label: RAVIN, wherever you work
items: Open Quick RAVIN from the ARROW controls without leaving the center you're using.
Move the floating conversation window around your workspace and resize it from any edge or corner.
Dock RAVIN to the left, right, top, or bottom of the screen.
Choose whether a docked conversation overlays your workspace or makes room by shifting the page.
Docking and movement use elastic animations, with reduced-motion alternatives.
Continue an account-scoped Quick RAVIN conversation as you navigate within the same browser tab.
Use the refreshed full RAVIN interface with identity-specific message layouts and conversation controls.
Access a full RAVIN command strip for new chats, search, tasks, calendar, and focus mode.

groups.label: Atlas
items: Atlas now participates in ARROW's five-identity appearance system.
Explore maps and connected information through redesigned layouts and canvas treatments.
Use improved map controls for selecting, focusing on, and navigating elements.
On smaller screens, open search and filters in a dedicated mobile drawer.
Map backgrounds, selection visuals, and controls respond to the active ARROW color choices.

groups.label: Relay and communication
items: Relay messaging now better matches the ARROW identity you choose.
Message bubbles, conversation rows, writing areas, and tool panels use tailored layouts across the non-Core identities.
Chat presentation has been refined without changing existing conversations or permissions.
Responsive messaging layouts make conversations and controls easier to use on smaller screens.
Updated styling, surfaces, and accents bring Relay's workspace closer to Orbit, Waypoint, and RAVIN.

groups.label: Navigation, access, and reliability
items: A shared Staff · Orbit · Dashboard control makes authorized staff tools more discoverable.
Staff remains role-gated for eligible owners, admins, and moderators.
The staff workspace has better scrolling and sizing, resolving the clipped owner dashboard area.
Orbit and Staff use coordinated directional transitions, with reduced-motion accommodations.
Cross-center navigation, account-aware preferences, and responsive layouts have received additional refinement.
Contrast and keyboard behavior have been improved in key menus, widgets, and dialogs.

groups.label: What’s New and update history
items: What’s New has moved from Relay into ARROW's own Workspace panel, where it's available across the suite.
The release announcement is shown once per signed-in account for this release, with your history always available in the panel.
Closing the announcement sends it into the ARROW panel with a compact animated transition.
The previous eleven Relay release entries remain available in the history below.

history.title: Relay 1.1 · ARROW Update
history.summary: Your daily workspace, connected to the complete ARROW suite with a refreshed RAVIN dashboard widget.

groups.label: RAVIN on your dashboard
items: Write a multiline question, organize a brain dump, or start planning your day from the refreshed RAVIN widget.
Questions open as drafts in RAVIN so you can review them before sending. Public and beta open their matching RAVIN workspace.

groups.label: Connected ARROW
items: The current integrated ARROW experience is available on public, including Orbit, Relay, Waypoint, Atlas, and RAVIN.
Request beta access from the public site, open the beta workspace when approved, and return to public from beta.

history.title: Relay 1.0.9 · Cleanup & Polish
history.summary: A recap of the cleanup work leading into 1.1: smoother navigation, simpler preferences, and more organized staff tools across ARROW.

groups.label: Everyday polish
items: Cleaned up keyboard shortcut behavior and simplified appearance preferences by removing the oversized color selection.
Improved shared navigation, layout behavior, and consistency between Relay and the other ARROW workspaces.

groups.label: Staff workspace
items: Moved staff controls into a dedicated Orbit workspace with clearer organization for owners, admins, and moderators.
Hardened role access and added owner experience previews for testing staff and normal-user views.

history.title: Relay 1.0.8
history.summary: Relay 1.0.8 brings the current beta experience to public, opens Orbit from Relay, and rolls in the latest stability and interface fixes.

groups.label: ARROW and navigation
items: Relay now opens Orbit from the ARROW control while public access stays scoped to Relay; Atlas, RAVIN, and Waypoint remain visible but unavailable for now.
Orbit navigation supports number shortcuts followed by Enter, and the shared ARROW control has been cleaned up to avoid duplicate mounts and clipped controls.

groups.label: Reliability and polish
items: The old Relay startup and duplicate full-page transition systems were removed so the app opens more reliably and avoids stacked animations.
Public and beta now use the same hardened Relay shell, with improved cache behavior, account loading, support tools, and layout fixes carried forward from beta.

history.title: Focus Update
history.summary: Relay 1.0.7 sharpens the daily workflow with Focus, cleaner communication and calendar layouts, safer connected-account handling, and a more adaptive dashboard.

groups.label: Focus and dashboard
items: Focus adds a dedicated workspace for timed work sessions and quick access to the parts of Relay that matter while you are working.
Dashboard widgets now change their internal layout for each selected size instead of relying on internal scrollbars.
Compact, skinny, tall, wide, and large widget sizes preserve the useful controls and information that fit each shape.

groups.label: Calendar, chats, and navigation
items: Calendar desktop spacing was tightened so all seven days remain visible without squeezing the main grid.
Chats use the available desktop width more effectively, Contacts sits beside Chats in navigation, and the dashboard is denser and easier to scan.
Mailbox access was removed from Relay while Calendar connections remain available through calendar-only permissions.

groups.label: Launch polish
items: Owner account inspection now uses the renamed Calendar integration data without exposing raw database errors in the interface.
The Relay mark now uses the same high-quality silver vector shading as the app icon.
Emergency Mode is no longer exposed on the public release and remains available only on the Beta channel.

history.title: Planning Update
history.summary: Relay 1.0.6 turns planning into a daily workflow with a real Schedule timeline, stronger Planner editing, and a more reliable dashboard experience.

groups.label: Schedule
items: Schedule adds a vertical daily timeline with week navigation, a live NOW line, and a clear view of the day on desktop and mobile.
Timed Google, Microsoft, and Relay Planner events appear as fixed commitments while personal blocks and scheduled To-Dos stay flexible.
Give To-Dos an estimated duration, keep unfinished work in the Unscheduled tray, then drag tasks onto the timeline or use Next spot to find an open block.
Create personal Focus, Break, Routine, or Personal blocks and move flexible blocks as the day changes.

groups.label: Planner
items: Plan creators can edit the plan name, notes, repeat pattern, weekdays, date range, and start/end times after creating it.
Custom-date plans use a compact month calendar where individual day boxes can be selected or removed with a click.
Editing preserves past occurrences and responses on unchanged future dates while only changing the future dates the creator actually edits.

groups.label: Dashboard and polish
items: Dashboard timing widgets now share live upcoming-event logic so Next Up, Today, School Schedule, and Countdowns stop showing timed events after they begin.
Dashboard Studio uses independent desktop scroll panes for the live preview and customization inspector, with its controls kept in reach.
Focus, Assignments, Weather, sunrise/sunset, and other non-RAVIN widgets received a functionality and stale-data audit; unsupported placeholder widgets were removed for now.
Sign-in now clearly asks for a personal account and warns against school-administered, work-managed, or other administrator-controlled email accounts.

history.title: Your Relay, your layout
history.summary: Relay 1.0.5 turns the dashboard into a real workspace, expands planning and Calendar intelligence, and gives desktop Relay more control without making mobile more complicated.

groups.label: Dashboard Studio
items: Customize the dashboard in a dedicated full-screen Studio with a persistent live preview.
Drag widgets to reorder them, drag hidden widgets onto the canvas, and resize width or height on a 12-column snap grid.
Use built-in layouts or save your own reusable dashboard presets, including widget visibility, order, width, and height.
The expanded widget library includes Weather, Quick Note, Focus, Assignments, Day Progress, School Schedule, RAVIN previews, and more.

groups.label: Planning and Calendar
items: Planner items can use real start and end times, and recurring plans present upcoming occurrences without cluttering the active view with past dates.
Planner creation, schedule summaries, occurrence selection, and overview cards are clearer and faster to scan.
Connected Google Calendar can discover subscribed and shared calendars, and all-day events stay truly all-day.

groups.label: Desktop and Still
items: Desktop Relay supports Classic, Focus Rail, Topbar, and Floating Dock layouts while mobile keeps its stable navigation model.
Still has been rebuilt as a quiet structured experience with visible navigation, restrained motion, subtle hierarchy, and sparse accent signals.
Still keyboard shortcuts are scoped to Still itself, and its experience controls are easier to discover and exit.

history.title: Make Relay yours
history.summary: Relay 1.0.4 brings the full Relay Experience system to public, expands color choices, improves particle continuity, and adds Emergency Mode as a resilient fallback.

groups.label: New
items: Relay Experience lets you switch between Flow, Still, Nexus, Aura, Slate, Spark, Lucid, and Vivid.
A much larger color palette includes additional single colors and two-color combinations.
Vivid uses the selected primary color across panels, controls, borders, and particles in multiple shades.
Emergency Mode provides a lightweight fallback for essential Relay access if the main interface has trouble loading.

groups.label: Improved
items: Landing, loading, and transition particles now keep your selected palette instead of snapping back to white.
Lucid keeps its glass depth without distorting panel geometry or clipping popovers.
Still and Slate keep controls readable on hover, and Slate adds the mouse-following sidebar accent rail.
The Experience picker is better organized and stays usable as the number of modes and palettes grows.

history.title: Notes arrive in Relay
history.summary: Relay 1.0.3 added a dedicated private Notes workspace and clearer staff identities.

groups.label: New
items: Notes have their own tab and sync privately with your Relay account.
Build notes from text, headings, lists, checkboxes, and quotes, with automatic saving, search, pinning, and block reordering.
Owner, Admin, and Moderator titles appear beside people across profiles, contacts, and chats.

groups.label: Foundation
items: Notes use structured blocks and stable IDs so a future visual knowledge graph can connect notes, tasks, and files for RAVIN.

history.title: A clearer Relay update
history.summary: Update history is built into Relay, returning users get a quick one-time update brief, and notification setup is easier to understand.

groups.label: New
items: What’s New keeps Relay updates in one easy-to-find place.
Returning users get a one-time summary after Relay updates.

groups.label: Improved
items: Notification setup reminds you to allow your browser in your device notification settings.
Release information uses simple wording instead of developer-style changelog language.

history.title: Public-release preparation
history.summary: Relay 1.0.1 served as the notification and stability checkpoint leading into the 1.0.2 public release.

groups.label: Release focus
items: Reliable device notifications for messages and requests.
Core messaging, planning, account, and navigation stability.
Final polish before opening Relay beyond the beta group.

history.title: Relay beta foundation
history.summary: The early Relay build established messaging, planning, connected services, profiles, and the core interface.

groups.label: Included
items: Messaging, contacts, planner, to-do, calendar, and account views.
Profiles, account controls, staff tools, and the Relay dashboard.
